# claude-bughunter

> A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **83 skills** · 15 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com).

Built by **Sachin Sharma** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

 
   SPONSORED BY 
   
   
     
       
       
     
   
      
   
     
       
       
     
   
 

---

## What is this?

`claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the Claude Code skills system. Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope.

Four layers stack:

- **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline.
- **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates.
- **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation.
- **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables.

All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name.

---

## Quickstart

**Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls
```

All 83 skills + 15 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`.

**A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them.

**Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git
cd Claude-BugHunter
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
bash scripts/install.sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1
```

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

   "大道至简" 
 

 

中文 | English

 

* 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
* MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
* 项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。
* MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion。
* 项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。
* 这不仅是一个大语言模型全阶段开源复现项目，也是一套面向 LLM 入门与实践的教程。
* 希望此项目能为更多人提供一个可复现、可理解、可扩展的起点，一起感受创造的乐趣，并推动更广泛 AI 社区的进步。

> 注：本项目基于 Apache 2.0 协议开源，完全免费。“2 小时” 指 SFT 阶段在单张 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 `1 epoch` 的实测耗时，“3 块钱” 指对应时段的 GPU 租用成本。

# 📌 项目介绍

大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出现，引发了全球范围内对 AI 的空前关注。无论是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 还是 Qwen，都以惊艳的效果让人真切感受到这场技术浪潮的冲击力。然而，动辄数百亿参数的模型规模，使得它们对个人设备而言不仅难以训练，甚至连部署都显得遥不可及。打开大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其内部运作机制，本应是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遗憾的是，绝大多数探索最终都止步于使用 LoRA 等技术对现有大模型做少量微调，学习一些新指令或特定任务。这更像是在教牛顿如何使用 21 世纪的智能手机——虽然有趣，却偏离了理解物理本质的初衷。

与此同时，第三方的大模型框架与工具库，如 `transformers` / `trl` / `peft` 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的接口。只需短短十几行代码，就可以完成“加载模型 + 加载数据集 + 推理 + 强化学习”的全流程训练。这种高效封装固然便利，却也在一定程度上把开发者与底层实现隔离开来，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心代码的机会。我认为 “用乐高自己拼出一架飞机，远比坐在头等舱里飞行更让人兴奋”，然而更现实的问题是，互联网上充斥着大量付费课程和营销内容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的讲解包装所谓的 AI 教程。正因如此，本项目的初衷就是尽可能降低 LLM 的学习门槛，让每个人都能从理解每一行代码开始，从 0 开始亲手训练一个极小的语言模型。是的，从**零开始训练**，而不是仅仅停留在**推理**层面。最低只需不到 3 块钱的服务器成本，就能亲身体验从 0 到 1 构建一个语言模型的全过程。

😊 一起感受创造的乐趣吧！

---

#### 🎉 本项目包含以下内容

- 提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 结构代码（Dense + MoE），当前主线结构对齐 `Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE` 生态。
- 提供 Tokenizer 与分词器训练代码，支持 ` `、` `、` ` 等模板标记。
- 覆盖 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等完整训练流程。
- 提供全阶段开源数据，覆盖收集、蒸馏、清洗与去重后的高质量数据集。
- 关键训练算法与核心模块均从 0 实现，不依赖第三方框架封装。
- 兼容 `transformers`、`trl`、`peft` 等主流框架，以及 `llama.cpp`、`vllm`、`ollama` 等常用推理引擎与 `Llama-Factory` 等训练框架。
- 支持单机单卡与单机多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）训练，支持 wandb / swanlab 可视化与动态启停训练。
- 支持在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方测评集上进行评测，并支持通过 YaRN 实现 RoPE 长文本外推。
- 提供兼容 OpenAI API 协议的极简服务端，便于接入 FastGPT、Open-WebUI 等第三方 Chat UI，并支持 `reasoning_content`、`tool_calls`、`open_thinking`。
- 提供基于 Streamlit 的极简聊天 WebUI，支持思考展示、工具选择与多轮 Tool Call。
- 包含实验性拓展：离散扩散语言模型（dLM）与线性注意力模型（Linear Attention），均可基于主线 AR 模型进行续训。

# Cursor plugins

# **🔥 Firecrawl**

**Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three.

- **Firecrawl Local.** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.
- **Firecrawl Cloud.** Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
- **Self-hosting.** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure.

_Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_

 
   
 

---

## Firecrawl Local

Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`.

```bash
cargo install firecrawl-local
```

If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

```bash
npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev
```

Scrape a page and print its markdown.

```bash
firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown
```

Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page.

```bash
firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages
```

List every URL on a site.

```bash
firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev
```

Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning.

### Add it to your AI agent

`init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer.

```bash
firecrawl-local init
```

Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud.

### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost

`serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.

```bash
firecrawl-local serve
```

NGINX (pronounced "engine x" or "en-jin-eks") is the world's most popular Web Server, high performance Load Balancer, Reverse Proxy, API Gateway and Content Cache.

NGINX is free and open source software, distributed under the terms of a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.

Enterprise distributions, commercial support and training are available from F5, Inc.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The goal of this README is to provide a basic, structured introduction to NGINX for novice users. Please refer to the full NGINX documentation for detailed information on installing, building, configuring, debugging, and more. These documentation pages also contain a more detailed Beginners Guide, How-Tos, Development guide, and a complete module and directive reference.

NGINX is installed software with binary packages available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions. See Tested OS and Platforms for a full list of compatible systems.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> While nearly all popular Linux-based operating systems are distributed with a community version of nginx, we highly advise installation and usage of official packages or sources from this repository. Doing so ensures that you're using the most recent release or source code, including the latest feature-set, fixes and security patches.

## Modules
NGINX is comprised of individual modules, each extending core functionality by providing additional, configurable features. See "Modules reference" at the bottom of nginx documentation for a complete list of official modules.

NGINX modules can be built and distributed as static or dynamic modules. Static modules are defined at build-time, compiled, and distributed in the resulting binaries. See Dynamic Modules for more information on how they work, as well as, how to obtain, install, and configure them.

nginx -V

items.summary: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
items.content:
Open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models.
 

 
   Documentation   •   Blog   •   Key Features   •   Tutorials   •   Integrations   •   Benchmarks   •   Generative AI  
 

[](https://badge.fury.io/py/openvino)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openvino-node)
[](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/openvino)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)

[](https://pepy.tech/project/openvino)
[](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/openvino/files)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)
  

- **Inference Optimization**: Boost deep learning performance in computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, natural language processing with large and small language models, and many other common tasks.
- **Flexible Model Support**: Use models trained with popular frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax. Directly integrate models built with transformers and diffusers from the Hugging Face Hub using Optimum Intel. Convert and deploy models without original frameworks.
- **Broad Platform Compatibility**: Reduce resource demands and efficiently deploy on a range of platforms from edge to cloud. OpenVINO™ supports inference on CPU (x86, ARM), GPU (Intel integrated & discrete GPU) and AI accelerators (Intel NPU).
- **Community and Ecosystem**: Join an active community contributing to the enhancement of deep learning performance across various domains.

Check out the OpenVINO Cheat Sheet and Key Features for a quick reference.

## Installation

Get your preferred distribution of OpenVINO or use this command for quick installation:

```sh
pip install -U openvino
```

### Verify Installation

After installation, you can verify OpenVINO is installed correctly by running:

```python
import openvino as ov
print(ov.__version__)
```

Check system requirements and supported devices for detailed information.

## Tutorials and Examples

OpenVINO Quickstart example will walk you through the basics of deploying your first model.

Learn how to optimize and deploy popular models with the OpenVINO Notebooks 📚:
- Create an LLM-powered Chatbot using OpenVINO
- YOLOv11 Optimization
- Text-to-Image Generation
- Multimodal assistant with LLaVa and OpenVINO
- Automatic speech recognition using Whisper and OpenVINO

Discover more examples in the OpenVINO Samples (Python & C++) and Notebooks (Python).

Here are easy-to-follow code examples demonstrating how to run PyTorch and TensorFlow model inference using OpenVINO:

**PyTorch Model**

```python
import openvino as ov
import torch
import torchvision

# load PyTorch model into memory
model = torch.hub.load("pytorch/vision", "shufflenet_v2_x1_0", weights="DEFAULT")

# convert the model into OpenVINO model
example = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
ov_model = ov.convert_model(model, example_input=(example,))

# compile the model for CPU device
core = ov.Core()
compiled_model = core.compile_model(ov_model, 'CPU')

# infer the model on random data

items.content: 为什么没有 AI 攻克医学难题的消息？是因为跨学科吗？ - V2EX Home Sign Up Sign In V2EX › 问与答 为什么没有 AI 攻克医学难题的消息？是因为跨学科吗？ shangrila · 6h 56m ago · 2230 views 计算机背后都是数学，所以数学难题很容易攻克，属于专业对口吗？ 那么医学背后是什么？为什么没有 AI 攻克癌症、慢病的一些好消息啊？ 医学 AI 跨学科 40 replies • 2026-11-22 14:48:17 +08:00 thinkm 6h 49m ago 1 ai 目前还是擅长纯电脑能干的活吧 医学涉及到临床，太复杂了 希望早点介入医学，我爸妈牙齿不太好，要是能研究出牙齿再生就好了 Pending 6h 47m ago 1 2 它连自身的灾难性遗忘和神经网络的可解释性问题都解决不了。 naythefirst01 6h 36m ago 3 等 A\的消息吧 iOCZS 6h 33m ago 4 因为人类对生理的了解还很少 jerseyhero 6h 28m ago 5 不是说 10 年内就攻克很多绝症么？希望 A\ 不要乱吹 NB Tink 6h 25m ago via iPhone 6 我只希望 A÷股价别先死了 KiriGiri 6h 21m ago 1 7 目前 AI 的 scaling 太弱了，还需要猛猛的 scaling，以前认为人脑一个神经元与大模型参数等价，最近有研究表明，单个人神经元就可以执行复杂运算，自身就可以相当于一个复杂神经网络，如果是这样，那人脑的参数量还要上升几个数量级。 Fading2276 6h 4m ago 8 @ thinkm 你的这个愿望有实现的可能了。 吃药长牙！日本开展全球首例临床试验 https://cn.nikkei.com/industry/scienceatechnology/55522-2024-05-07-14-30-00.html Shing 6h 4m ago 9 要找志愿者，签生死状的那种，且亲属不准事后扯皮，国家层面不准远程施法。 thinkm 6h 0m ago 10 @ Fading2276 666 phrack 5h 59m ago 2 11 它怎么解决医学难题 它就是设计的再快，也得等临床试验，而药物对人体的副作用，长期有效性，只能靠等时间到了才能知道 药物设计从来就不是成本最高的地方 --- 这些所谓的 frontier AI lab 做出来机器人之前，不要考虑他们能多大程度的推动医学，看到新闻当放屁就行了 机器人好歹能按月迭代，甚至按天迭代，医学至少也是按年来迭代的 之所以在编码和数学，甚至理论物理/理论化学，都有可能有重大推进，因为他们能在电脑的虚拟环境中无限按秒迭代 Planarians 5h 59m ago 12 有啊 癌症靶向药现在基本都靠 ai 设计了 以前都是人工一个个试过去 现在直接让 ai 就能设计 只是你不关注罢了 phrack 5h 54m ago 13 中国有 1/10 的乙肝患者，拿乙肝来举例吧 最新的药物是 gsk836，有 30%的临床治愈率，但是很重要的另外一个数据是：已经实现乙肝功能性治愈的患者，停用全部乙肝药物后，约 91% 在一年时仍能维持功能性治愈。而早期 IIb 期试验中，少量患者已经维持了长达 3 年。 你可以问问你认识的乙肝患者，后面这几个数据重要不重要 这几个数据，AI 能预测吗，能设计吗 superjojo 5h 46m ago 14 外行就别讨论了，既不懂医学，也不懂 AI guanhui07 5h 41m ago 15 临床还是复杂的 unused 5h 39m ago via Android 16 数学是形式科学，物理化学大部分属于自然科学，医学大部分属于应用科学 l353443703 5h 39m ago via Android 17 猜你在找，2024 年诺贝尔化学奖（AlphaFold） IndexOutOfBounds 5h 0m ago 18 @ phrack 赞同 我的理解就是验证成本高，设计 - 观察验证 - 反馈迭代，一套周期下来很长 相反，计算机 run 一下就完了 coderluan 4h 57m ago 19 数学先有猜想，然后有大量的人去尝试证明，只不过进度很慢，AI 也是去证明，但是进度飞快。但是对大部分医学问题，这个猜想就不存在，根本不知道原理，就谈不上证明了。不过也有存在类似"猜想"的问题，比如蛋白质结构，这个基本就是 AI 攻克的，人之前也能做，但是龟速，AI 直接全给算出来了，2024 年诺贝尔化学奖就是这个。 osilinka 4h 38m ago 20 有应用吧 只是这个行业太难了，尽管 dalio 那个 B 一直在吹牛逼，实际上网上很多的专业人士已经打脸了 18k 4h 31m ago via Android 21 有啊 现在各大药企管线研发都用到 AI 的 NetworkManager 4h 16m ago 22 你设计的再快 不需要实验吗 实验不需要时间吗 然后你以为你 XX 疫苗呢 直接给你打 anteros 4h 14m ago 23 除某些特殊时期的特殊情况以外。 一款药物或者疫苗的上市，都需要经过多年的实验和数据及审核，才能用到面世用到人身上的。 AI 能加快药物的研发，但是实验数据和跟踪观察 AI 很难提速。 MarcusCliff 4h 10m ago 24 未来能接住 AI 这个盘子的就是生物医药啊，难道过几年一年建几百 GW 的数据中心全拿去写代码吗 K3v1Nz 4h 7m ago 25 没法做到像软件工程一样端到端开发和测试或者像数学一样闭环验证，迭代会很慢的 Lykr 4h 6m ago 26 因为卡点在人，医学属于 human in the loop 的领域，只有能够 human out of the loop 的领域才能通过 LLM 使效率得到数量级的提升。 fatigue 4h 3m ago 27 你以为中医呢，脑袋一拍一个方子，包治百病 akring 3h 48m ago 28 用了估计也不敢宣传吧 signalas1 3h 41m ago 29 早晚的事 naeco 3h 32m ago 30 我理解是需要时间验证，药是给人吃的，疗效和副作用一时半会看不出来 ndxxx 2h 58m ago via Android 31 先问有没有，强国的国民真神企业，华为，早已经开始利用 AI 赋能医药业了。 华为市场营销出身的药物业务总裁，樊杰，2026 年 10 月在某个医药行业交流会上，名台场面来了。 提到药企原本做分子筛选、虚拟仿真这类干实验，普遍周期 4 周，短期目标是压缩到 1 周。此时樊杰抛出反问：为什么不能是一天，甚至一小时？ 理论上「干实验」确实可以缩短时间，但华为这家企业，「只管往别人家里下蛋」，「捞了好处就跑」这个信任危机从任正非开始，余承东发扬光大以后，大家早就怕啦😁 zhanying 2h 57m ago via Android 32 快进到 AI 为了研究医学开始抓捕人类进行人体实验 issues 2h 50

懒得弄转区，99 刀一年的正规付费 gemini pro 感觉应该是最便宜的了

1. 运动习惯的养成 每天，Apple Watch 都会提醒你完成运动圆环，从 Apple Watch 购买至今，我的每天目标是：活动 350 千卡、锻炼 30 分钟，站立 12 小时。刚才看了一眼，我已经累计合上所有圆环 2144 次（当天三个圆环全部合上） ![9B00062A-0E87-43F5-A3D9-96CAF23914E3_1_105_c.jpeg](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/03-9B00062A-0E87-43F5-A3D9-96CAF23914E3-1-105-c.jpg) 最开始，只是为了完成任务，获得勋章，有时候被提醒，就顺便多运动一下。但是慢慢的，这就变成了潜移默化的习惯，我会主动关注今天哪个指标没完成。 而到了傍晚，手表也会主动提示当天运动量不够，无数次，下雨天或者周末的夜晚，我都被这个提醒推出了房间，去户外散步，完成目标；而为了完成 12 小时站立的任务，白天，每隔 1 小时，会尽量让自己站起来活动 1-2 分钟，这也避免了在工位长时间的久坐 ![6AFC2158-64FB-41A5-B9BE-F39940F27784.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/04-6AFC2158-64FB-41A5-B9BE-F39940F27784.png) ![3A4FB886-1F6F-4300-B5F5-4990A4DF4EC1_4_5005_c.jpeg](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/05-3A4FB886-1F6F-4300-B5F5-4990A4DF4EC1-4-5005-c.jpg) 每个月的第一天，手表会推送一个月度挑战，基于你历史的运动数据，会给你一个需要努力一点才可以达到的目标，比如每个月跑步 6 次、本月闭合所有圆环 16 次 是的，就这样，长年累月，它慢慢影响着改变着我的每一天，而我收获了一堆奖章 ![0FDFDE38-FB55-4518-96F4-AFF9F955121A.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/06-0FDFDE38-FB55-4518-96F4-AFF9F955121A.png) ## 2. 健康监测 每天早晨醒来，我第一件事就是查看手表的睡眠评分。它会通过“睡眠时长”“就寝时间”“中断时间”三个维度，对整个夜晚的睡眠质量打分 如果发现分数持续不足 90 分，我会调整我的睡眠作息和节奏，也会相应的减少当天的运动量，中午会多午休一会，晚上早点入睡 而最新 apple watch ultra 4 和 12 系列，支持“准备指数”功能：它会根据近期运动量、生命体征（心率、呼吸频率、体温、血氧、心率变异性）、睡眠质量，来综合提供每日评分，而且还会实时动态调整分数，对于运动爱好者，可以参考这个评分，来调整自己的运动计划。 如果我发现指数不足 5 分，就会放弃跑步，选择休息 不止于此，它还支持血氧、心电图、摔倒监测、车祸监测、紧急 SOS 联络这些功能 ## 3. AI+苹果健康数据 当我累计了 8 年的数据，连接 AI 之后，我每周会让 AI 帮我自动生成健康周报，提供下一周的建议。有时候，我还会让 AI 分析我的某些指标最近几年的变化，比如心率、睡眠。 比如这周我跑了 3 次，一共 22.3 公里，但每天平均比前一周少睡了约 22 分钟...后面我也会单独再写一篇如何用 ai 来使用苹果健康数据 ![Pasted image 20261121224536.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/07-Pasted-image-20261121224536.png) ## 4. 便捷和人性化的功能 **a. 抬起手腕，就可以设置提醒和倒计时，再也不用拿出手机** 作为 j 人，吃牛肉火锅，我都需要定时涮牛肉，抬起手表”倒计时 1min“；丰巢快递总是忘拿，还要交钱“siri，明天提醒我拿快递”，洗了衣服忘记晾“30 分钟后提醒我晾衣服”，随时定个闹钟“给我设置一个明早 7 点的闹钟”，这些小场景，每天使用下来，节约了不少时间 **b. 丰富的免费表盘** 自带大量精美的免费表盘，设置小组件后，抬起手表，一眼可以查看大量的信息。比如现在我使用的表盘： 左侧可以看到我的 5 个核心指标是否正常（心率、呼吸频率、体温、血氧、心率变异性），右侧可以看到运动负荷是否超标（图中可以看到偏高了）。左上角是实时紫外线系数，中间是身体准备指数，而右上角是支付宝付款码，底部是运动圆环闭合情况，还有下一个闹钟的时间+倒计时工具。当然，这些小组件，都可以自定义，根据自己的需要设置不同的功能 ![incoming-03464FA4-1425-4FB4-A394-5614D9C5963C.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/08-incoming-03464FA4-1425-4FB4-A394-5614D9C5963C.png) ![407DF58C-6B80-436E-AD73-07782895A040.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/09-407DF58C-6B80-436E-AD73-07782895A040.png) **c. 生态联动**：搭配 iPhone，手机的通知会自动流转到手表，无缝切换，非常的丝滑 **d. 设置交通卡和 Apple pay**，不用掏手机，可以刷手表乘坐公交，在国外使用 Apple pay 支付也非常方便 **e. 搭配自带播客或者小宇宙 APP**，不带手机，戴着耳机和手表，就可以出门跑步 ![8C4EAC87-66A6-4D23-A5D0-CE2B548CCCA0.png](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/10-8C4EAC87-66A6-4D23-A5D0-CE2B548CCCA0.png) **f. 没有铃声的闹钟**：当手表设置为静音，手表会通过震动来唤醒你，不会打扰到别人。在早晨起床的时候，更加无感，也不会像闹钟声音那样刺耳，让人不适 当然，它最大的缺点就是续航，数字系列，只能 1 天左右，ultra 系列 2-3 天，相比一些专业运动手表，确实差了一些。 至于价格，有些人觉得很贵，就我自己的这几年更新迭代来看，旧表可以二手回收，新手表在双 11 或者 618 买入，年均持有成本可以做到 300～500 块钱（我 3 年以旧换新的计算）。 比如之前的 Apple Watch Ultra 2，是花 4000 块买的。戴了快两年半，最后 2650 块卖掉，算下来一共花了 1350 块，平均每个月 46 块钱。以我每天都戴的频率，再考虑到它给你的健康带来的改变，以及生活的便利性的提升，还是很挺值的 所以，这就是 apple watch，一个可以兼顾你的运动、健康，又提升生活品质的产品。 如果说除了手机之外，哪一款数码产品对我最重要，我觉得那就是 apple watch 了，也强烈推荐你购买一款智能手表，开始关注自己的健康 ![C6CD1DE7-F5CB-4D65-98F9-3B035FC2D8B1_1_201_a.jpeg](https://blog.scond.me/img/article-studio/2026-11-22-02-Apple-Watch-%E6%88%B4%E4%BA%868%E5%B9%B4-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E6%B5%8B%E8%AF%84/11-C6CD1DE7-F5CB-4D65-98F9-3B035FC2D8B1-1-201-a.jpg) If you haven’t read it, you can get a copy here . I have had the chance to use the new Claude Fable 5.2 quite a bit before its public launch 1 , and it is very impressive, following on the already excellent Opus 5.5. AI has gotten so good, in fact, that it is worth asking if Anthropic’s newest models (and the inevitable competing models OpenAI and Google will soon release) cross the boundary into being an Artificial General Intelligence? AGI is a much-debated term with a lot of potential definitions. For this post, I’ll go with: “an AI as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks you can do with a computer.” This explicitly excludes a lot of human work, including interacting with the physical world and other people, as well as most actual jobs, where “using a computer” is just one task among many. Still, even with these caveats, building a limited form of AGI has long been the goal of AI developers. So as not to keep you in suspense, I think the answer is that this is “almost” AGI, or what I have called Jagged AGI. Even within my limited definition, there are still important areas in many tasks where AI is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability. But the jaggedness is no longer about simple errors or hallucinations, which makes it harder to describe. So I want to try to do that in this post by showing you what Fable can do and where the gaps are. To get started I asked the new model: “I write OneUsefulThing among other stuff, I need you to create the most impressive thing I can share with people when you launch. It needs to be embeddable in a post and i can preface it however you like. it needs to have a visceral impact on people to show what you can do and the range of capabilities. It should grab them quickly. Be amazingly clever about this.” Fable asked me not to reveal anything until you had watched its video to the end. This was in one shot, with no feedback from me beyond the prompt. There is creativity here (including in the twist ending) and judgment and playfulness and cleverness. items.content: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) - by Ethan Mollick One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) My new book is out today... what happened since the last one Ethan Mollick Oct 20, 2026 820 148 70 Share My second book on AI, Co-Existence, is out today (and you can get it here ), 30 months after the release of Co-Intelligence in early 2024. Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts. Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. In the current era of agentic AI that I cover in Co-Existence , I delegated the work and let the AI handle it. In this case, I used Opus 5.5 in Claude Projects, which allows you to talk to a single “orchestrator” agent that then spins off additional agents as needed, giving them instructions and relaying information back to you. Getting the work done was straightforward. I gave the AI a couple sentences of suggestions and it did what would have taken me hours of work (all the research, all the graphing, all the layouts, all the images, all the citations…) in minutes. And since I didn’t have to do the work, I had the AI make many options for me. I picked some and gave handwavy reactions to others that would drive a human team mad (“make it better”). It even caught that I’d gotten the math wrong. I was going to call this post “28 months on the exponential.” Some examples of interacting with Claude to make the graphics for this post. Notice that it corrected me. “This is the worst AI you will ever use” I wrote this in my last book on AI, and it has continued to be literally true at every moment since. From early 2023 through early 2024, there was a single AI model that was undeniably the best in the world: GPT-4 from OpenAI. This was the AI model that most people remember from the first couple years of AI use, it was the one I thought about while writing Co-Intelligence , and it was the one that gave ChatGPT its status as the default AI for many people. Since then, twenty different AI models have held the lead at one time or another, all from Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI. Which company had the best AI model in the world. But the changing lead alone hides an even bigger change. A total of 180 AI models are now better than GPT-4 was at its release, many of which are open weights models, which anyone is free to use or modify. Nineteen of them can run on a modern smartphone. In the last year I have been posting about how I suspected that humans would have to approach working with agents as a manager, deciding how to delegate work to agents and specifying how those agents should be organized. I thought that getting agents to work effectively as a group would take careful construction, akin to building a company, and that this would take time to figure out. Nope. I fell prey to The Bitter Lesson, the hard truth, learned over and over again, that things that we thought required elaborate human rules and thinking can be solved with the brute force of better machine learning systems and more AI. The Bitter Lesson is everywhere among AI startups and companies adopting AI. A huge amount of effort went into building elaborate computer systems to feed AIs the right information at the right time, but AI systems have learned to seek out information themselves. The same thing happened to prompting. People built elaborate templates and chains of prompts that walked the AI through a task one step at a time. Then newer models turned out to be better at planning the steps themselves, and, as our research shows , planning steps have much less value. The history of the Bitter Le— — you know what? I don’t really need to explain the Bitter Lesson, I asked Claude to do it in a music video. With one prompt, Fable wrote the lyrics and submitted it to Suno; Opus 5.5 did everything else using code alone without any image generation (How did Opus 5.5 pull this off? The Bitter Lesson tells you!). I gave no feedback at all. As somebody who teaches managers and has published research on management, I guess I believed that managing agents would be different. Humans have been working on management for a very long time without fully figuring it out. It seemed like the kind of thing that would need to be designed by people, at least for a while. Nov 19, 2026 45 1 2 Share The other day my wife was chatting with AI. P.s. The full interactive version of this post is here . So let’s overlook the actual impossibilities and find out. Before we do the maths, people have been trying versions of this for 256 years. Nearly all of them shut down or got caught. None of them came close to today’s scale. So what would it actually take? Let’s be generous. Assume everyone types at world-record speed, 200 words a minute, non-stop. Everyone is happy to wait 10 minutes for a reply. And it’s a remote company spread across every time zone, so someone is always awake. The average ChatGPT user sends about 4 messages a day, and a reply is roughly 500 words now. With over a billion people using the big AI chatbots, that’s about 6 billion messages every day. 10.4 million people typing at world-record speed, round the clock, with no sleep, no lunch, and no days off. Okay, let’s run it like a real company instead. Which means it needs a CEO. Me. 11.8 billion internal messages a day, just to keep the place running. Oh, and we still have to answer the 6 billion messages people actually sent us. All in, you’d need 77.4 million staff just to keep 10.4 million people typing at any given moment. If you want to check my maths: a 40-hour week, time off from a 2025 survey of UK call centres , 12.1 people per manager ( the US average ), and 2 HR people per 100 staff ( SHRM ). People quit at the US rate , earn the US median for customer service , and get 153 chat messages a day , like the average Microsoft Teams user. The biggest Zoom call holds 1 million . More people won’t work. But what about a guessing game from 1950, played by a mathematician called Claude Shannon? Yes, Claude. He picked a line from a book, hid it from his wife Betty, and got her to guess it one letter at a time. Betty didn’t know the sentence, she just knew the patterns of English. My wife does this to me every day. She’s had years of practice. So what if we replaced Betty with a computer? For more than 60 years, the answer was no. Giving machines more to read barely helped, because they could only see the last couple of words. Try guessing what comes after “speak fluent…” with no other clues. In 2017, eight people at Google let it see every word at once and weigh the ones that matter, like France. They called that attention, and the machine a transformer. It’s the T in ChatGPT. Suddenly, giving it more to read actually worked. More text, bigger brain, better guesses. Writing a reply is the same thing. It reads what you said and guesses the next word, or piece of a word (called a token), sticks it on the end, looks back at everything again, and guesses the next one. items.content: Productiv-icky - by Ben Tossell - Ben's Bites Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Productiv-icky Digging holes on the beach Ben Tossell Nov 17, 2026 79 4 1 Share productiv-icky (adj.) - the feeling of doing work you didn’t mean to do We have a problem. full interactive post is here We agree this is insane, right? Someone I don’t know sends me emails that I’m expected to reply to. I don’t know them. I don’t work for them. So I ignore them (well actually I send them to email jail). Nuh-uh, that’s not my work, buddy. But it’s different if it’s my super-intelligent, helpful agent friend… Yeses are easy. They’re quick. But every yes has a yes-tax. The hidden extra work you didn’t think of. The long tail of regret where you question why you ever said yes. Say I did reply to those emails, they’d send me stuff to read to show how great they are at their job and how much better I’d be. Then we’d organise a call (which would derail whichever day that call was on). Then we’d have follow-up items. Then a string of other crap I couldn’t care less about. I know what’s going to happen. I can smell it, it stinks. I’ve said yes and paid the tax many times before. Now I pay $200/mo for a super-intelligent, over-eager, needy little nerd to ping me incessantly about taking things off my plate. I feel bad for him. He wants to work. He’s gagging for it. Just. One. More. Task. Master. Plus, my little nerd has a gambling problem. Or rather, he feeds mine. Remember years ago sending tons of Slack messages to get the most out of your $20/mo plan? Nor me. Why? Because it’s dumb. But now we feel like we should use all our tokens before they run out. Why? Because everyone else is. We started measuring shovels instead of the hole. Someone’s needy little nerd booked their dentist, replied to their mum and launched a business whilst they were asleep. They’ve got an org chart. For nerds. With a Chief of Staff. You feel behind. Like way behind. So you grab a shovel and start digging. A little hole over there to triage your inbox, one here to draft your tweets, one to check on those. Then you spend your day checking the holes are being dug right. Before long, you’re surrounded by holes and a mountain of dirt you gotta do something with. Now as a man, holes are hardwired into my DNA. A few beers, a beach and a shovel, I’m digging a hole. I’d take pride in it. I’d make the best one, impressively round, deep enough to see sea water seep through the bottom. But I’d only dig one. There’s a whole beach but I chose this spot. Next time the needy little nerd pings you: do you really want another hole? Also, don’t dig big holes on the beach. They collapse. My Ramp post was really well received with one or two ‘I’m not sure what I just looked at’ comments (which is totally fair). The best I can describe what I’m doing now is exploring people and companies who are having fun with AI, doing things differently, being authentic and succeeding . Which is basically how I want to describe my ‘work’. But I think a lot of people are living in fear. Scared they’re behind, they’re not doing enough, others using AI ‘better’ than them, where’s there job going etc. I want to focus on using AI for fun. AI is a tool, you need one agent app (I’ve been using Droid with Opus 5.5 medium, fast mode for my posts, fable here and there). Use the tool to do work beyond what you could do before, don’t think about how you can finally optimise every aspect of every little thing. (I’ve basically stopped using Grok Bot, except telling me when the tennis is on). As part of my explorations I’m working on a new post for another company I admire and who do things very differently. Coming next week… “Everyone judges a book by its cover” Can you guess which company it is? And yes, these animations are staying. Honestly I love them. I love making them too. So much so that I set up a sophisticated camera set up to monitor what my days look like and here’s the footage. Morning voice dump. Kids. Stickmen. Nathan Lambert Nov 14, 2026 122 24 20 Share Article voiceover 0:00 -7:28 Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on. Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up. Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Subscribe In this period, the open model economy is in its nascency. These are crucial years for establishing use-cases, revenue flow, and motives to continue training the next generation models. I discussed the sensitivity of these early years in my recent talk at Fireworks Forge ( slides , recording ). The core of the argument is one upside for open models, a reason to be optimistic, and one downside. The positive case is that the open model economy has correctly latched onto “ownership of intelligence” and enterprise post-training as a crucial lane. What is to be determined is exactly how big the downstream market is. The downside is that the true long-term benefit of open models, as truly commoditized intelligence, is very far from realization with compute in such short supply. In the near term, where inference startups are also struggling to get enough chips (because Anthropic and OpenAI are buying so much capacity), there’s little margin competition on open-weight models. If open-source models are also served at giant inference margins, as we learned with DeepSeek’s DeepInfer release, they’re far from a commodity. In this paradigm, the closed labs with better economies of scale and integration from model to datacenter and chips will win. I expanded on this challenge in my recent piece on the open model economy . Together, a lot still needs to go right for open models to be a meaningful economic engine.
